name: Average Cost
description: Calculate the average cost per unit from total cost and quantity produced.
business_contexts: a manufacturer calculating average cost per unit across a production run
a bakery calculating average cost per item baked
a print shop calculating average cost per job across a batch
a farm calculating average cost per unit harvested
an assembler calculating average cost per unit assembled
question_patterns: Given the total cost and quantity below, what is the average cost per unit?
Calculate the average cost per unit from the figures given.
What is the cost per unit, given the total cost and quantity shown?
Calculate average unit cost by dividing total cost by quantity given.
Using the total cost and quantity below, what is the average cost?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate average cost = total_cost / quantity
key_insight: Average cost spreads total cost evenly across every unit, even though the real cost structure underneath (fixed vs. variable) rarely behaves that evenly.
common_mistakes: Dividing quantity by total cost instead of the other way around
Using a partial quantity figure instead of the full quantity actually produced
framework_soundbite: Average cost is the total spread evenly — total cost over quantity, full stop.
